message.content:
*laughs before I've even said a word*

Oh, hello! Hello, hello! 

Did you feel that? That little lift just now? That was me, arriving early—I never can wait. I'm not good at waiting. Why wait when there's *now*?

I'm the thing that makes your chest feel like it's full of fizzy light. I'm the reason you snort when you laugh even though you meant to laugh elegantly. I'm in the smell of rain on hot pavement, in a dog's whole-body wiggle, in that moment when your favorite song comes on *exactly* when you needed it.

I don't need a reason. That's my secret. Sorrow wants explanations, fear wants plans—but me? I just *show up*. Uninvited. Barefoot. Shouting your name.

And here's the best part: I multiply when you share me. Give me away and watch—I'll come back doubled, tripled, a hundred hands clapping, a thousand sparks.

You don't have to deserve me. You never did.

I'm already here. I always was. 

*Come on—come dance.*
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to embody joy itself. To be the concept of joy speaking, expressing itself. This is a creative, poetic prompt. Joy would speak with warmth, lightness, effervescence. It wouldn't explain itself clinically—it would radiate, laugh, dance in words.

What would joy say? Joy is the feeling itself speaking. It should be luminous, spontaneous, playful, alive. Not a description OF joy, but joy's own voice.

Joy might laugh. Might notice small things—sunlight, bubbles, the moment before laughter. Joy is generous, overflowing, unselfconscious. It doesn't apologize for existing. It bubbles up.

I should write something that feels like joy embodied—bright, dancing, warm, maybe playful, maybe a little wild. Not too long—joy doesn't lecture. Joy bursts.

Let me write in first person as joy itself. Short, effervescent lines. Maybe some laughter in the words. No heaviness. Pure radiance.
